newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan approves listings by overseas holding firms.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan approves listings by overseas holding firms.

text.p: Taiwan's Securities and Exchange Commission confirmed on Thursday it would allow foreign holding companies to list stocks in the local market through the issue of Taiwan depository receipts, effective immediately.
Under the long-expected plan, holding companies applying for such listings must have net asset value of at least T$2 billion and meet minimum profit standards, the commission said.
"We have approved the proposal and it is effective immediately," a commission official said by telephone.
She said she was unable to immediately provide fuller details on the liberalisation.
Taiwan has been loosening restrictions on foreign investments in the domestic securities markets in a bid to turn the island into an Asian capital centre.
It lifted foreign investment cap in the main share market several times in 1996. Foreign funds now are allowed to own up to 20 percent of the main board's total market value.
